doc.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

chapter: Swing Street shows and the business
title: Storytelling to break down the wall between player and audience
summary: He argues that narrating the music makes audiences feel part of it, as in classical concerts, and provides work for players.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

Which I believe, the music that I believe in was. Whether some music works better with — you’re in awe of that great performer. But I think even the great ones, Andre Watts is a wonderful, he knows classical music. He knows why he’s going to pick a program and do this tune and do this one and this one led from here to here. All of a sudden the audience can share so much more with you. So that’s where “The Magic of Swing Street” came in, in the face of whether — you know I just decided I was going to do it. And everybody has fun doing it. And it provides a lot of work for guys.
